key_provisions.summary_own_words: General prohibition on agreements or collusion about production, supply, distribution, storage or acquisition of goods/services that harm competition.
Lists practices presumed to harm competition (e.g., price fixing, output limits, market sharing, bid rigging).
Addresses tie-in, exclusive supply, exclusive distribution, refusal to deal and resale price maintenance arrangements.
Carves out certain acts from the prohibition (read text for exact scope).
Prohibits abuse of dominance; s.16(2) lists presumed abuses (e.g., unfair/discriminatory pricing, predatory pricing below cost, limiting production or access).
Commission's pre-inquiry and inquiry procedure on complaints or its own initiative.
Interim orders to stop conduct that appears to breach ss.15-16 during the process.
Financial penalties; secondary sources cite up to 10% of average turnover (3 years) or up to three times profit for cartel conduct. Confirm against text.
Sources conflict on whether s.21 covers combinations or agreements made outside Bangladesh. MUST check the text before citing.
Establishes the Bangladesh Competition Commission.
Elements of a valid contract: free consent, competent parties, lawful consideration and object.
Defines free consent; consent induced by coercion, undue influence, fraud, misrepresentation or mistake is not free.
Contracts obtained through dominant position over the other party's will.
Consideration or object is unlawful if forbidden by law, defeats law, is fraudulent or opposed to public policy.
Agreements restraining a lawful profession, trade or business are void (limited exception for sale of goodwill). Key hook for non-competes and exclusivity.
Agreements restricting enforcement of rights through ordinary legal proceedings are void to that extent (arbitration carve-out).
Compensation for loss naturally arising from breach; no remote or indirect loss.
Where a sum is named for breach, courts award reasonable compensation not exceeding the named amount.
Defines contract of indemnity (relevant to liability allocation clauses).
Implied conditions/warranties on title, description, quality/fitness and sample.
Express terms can negate or vary implied terms (check exact wording).
Prohibits contracts, combinations and conspiracies in restraint of trade; criminal and civil enforcement.
Prohibits monopolization, attempts and conspiracies to monopolize.
Unlawful to sell/lease goods on condition of not dealing with competitors where effect may substantially lessen competition or tend to create monopoly.
Private right of action with threefold damages and attorney's fees.
Prohibits acquisitions that may substantially lessen competition.
Restricts price discrimination between competing purchasers of like goods with competitive injury.
Declares unfair methods of competition and unfair or deceptive acts unlawful.
Court may refuse to enforce unconscionable contracts or clauses.
Contractual limits on remedies and consequential damages allowed unless unconscionable or remedy fails of essential purpose.
Rules for excluding or modifying implied warranties (conspicuousness etc.).
Liquidated damages valid only if reasonable in light of anticipated or actual harm.
Good-faith duties in requirements/output contracts; exclusive dealing implies best efforts.
Prohibits agreements, decisions and concerted practices that restrict competition and affect trade between Member States.
Prohibited agreements are automatically void.
Conditions for exemption (efficiencies, consumer benefit, indispensability, no elimination of competition).
Prohibits abuse of a dominant position (unfair prices, limiting production, discrimination, tying).
Resale price maintenance and certain territorial/customer restrictions remove block-exemption benefit.
Non-compete obligations exceeding five years or post-term non-competes are not exempted (limited exceptions).
Fines up to 10% of total turnover for infringements of Arts. 101-102.
Concentrations that significantly impede effective competition are incompatible with the internal market.
